Question: Why does the sky appear blue? Answer in one clear short paragraph:
The reason is that the sun's rays are bluer than they are redder. Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. The shorter wavelengths (blue) scatter more easily, and the longer wavelengths (red) less easily. So we see more blue light than red. When sunlight passes through a lot of water vapor, it gets scattered more by the smaller water molecules than by the larger air molecules. That is why the sky has a bluish tint.�On a cloudy day, if you look at the sky, you will find that it appears to be white because there is no longer any scattered light from the sun or moon which can produce a blue tint. It becomes lighter because of this effect alone!
